clue.text: Punish the wretched bard discovering this American songster!

parts.note: to whip someone is to punish them
poor, as in 'the poor fellow', means wretched
the Bard is Shakespeare, whose first name was Will

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging that a miserable poet be punished for discovering a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bard' is the usual name for William Shakespeare, so the bard gives WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippoorwill is a North American nightjar named for its call, so a singing bird of that continent.

clue.text: One I watch out for in Kansas

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone warning about the thing they keep an eye out for in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city of the US state of Kansas.

clue.text: Got a touch off by frenzied dieting

indicators.note: frenzied means wild and disordered, so the letters of dieting are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone driven to fury by a crash diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch off a fire or fuse is to set it alight, so the past tense is a set-alight synonym.

clue.text: Teaching a lesson in being generous

definitions.meaning: to pay someone out is to punish them or get revenge
spending money freely, handing it over

explanation.surface: Lavish generosity as a way of instructing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay out means both to take revenge on someone and to spend or disburse money freely.

clue.text: Work with credit say out of sight

indicators.note: say means the words are heard rather than spelt, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: work is OP (opus) and credit is TICK, as in buying on tick, giving OP-TICK

explanation.surface: A job paid on credit that has slipped out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for an opus and TICK for credit (buy on tick) together are said like the answer; 'out' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is the adjective for the eye and vision, so pertaining to seeing.

clue.text: Feller like Davy Crockett

definitions.meaning: a frontier backwoodsman of American legend

explanation.surface: A chap described as resembling the frontier hero Davy Crockett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' reads as slang for a fellow but means one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodman cuts timber in forests, and Crockett was a famed frontiersman of the wild woods.

clue.text: Untie hair for wash-out

definitions.meaning: to release tied-up hair so it falls loose

explanation.surface: Loosening one's hairdo before washing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is let down when untied, and a letdown is a flop or disappointment.

clue.text: Clearly a top-liner competition

definitions.meaning: a ship that is the champion, the best of liners
a contest to find the best

explanation.surface: Something obviously at the head of the bill in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship is a tournament, and split it reads as champion ship, a leading liner.

clue.text: Horse and carriage?

definitions.meaning: a breed of high-stepping riding or driving horse

explanation.surface: A question about a horse and the vehicle it pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is both a light trotting horse and a hired coach or cab.

clue.text: Pair to stage dance

parts.note: a pair is two
a stage in a process is a step

explanation.surface: A couple about to put on a dance performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance in duple time.

clue.text: Fitting attire for high-flyers

parts.note: reads as smart clothes for ambitious people, but means gear for those flying at altitude

explanation.surface: Suitable dress for ambitious executives.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots and astronauts at great height wear an inflatable garment keeping air pressure around the body.

clue.text: Damp mines to be modified

indicators.note: be modified means the letters of mines and to are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A plan to alter mines so they are flooded.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten is to wet slightly, a verb sense of damp.

clue.text: Settle score

explanation.surface: An instruction to resolve a dispute or tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Compose means both to calm or settle oneself and to write a musical score.

clue.text: Sorcerer decapitated mountain goat

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a sorcerer is a wizard

explanation.surface: A magician beheaded a goat in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope of high peaks.

clue.text: Those against being sent on pop revival

indicators.note: a revival remakes something, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Critics who object to old pop songs being sent out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents are adversaries, people ranged on the other side.

clue.text: Item -a capital plot

parts.note: Para was the former name of Belem, capital of the Brazilian state of Para
a graph is a plot of values

explanation.surface: A news item about a conspiracy in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Belem in Brazil, a state capital, was long known simply as Para.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper item or short piece of text in a list is a paragraph.

clue.text: One on top in some vulgar part

definitions.text: One on top in some vulgar part

parts.words: One on top in some vulgar part
parts.note: sounds rude, but a vulgar fraction is an ordinary fraction and this is its upper figure

explanation.surface: A risque hint about a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In a common fraction the figure above the line is the numerator.

clue.text: He painted the heartless Dickensian doctor

parts.note: Edouard Manet was a French painter

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the is removed

explanation.surface: An artist painting a cruel doctor from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Manette is a character in A Tale of Two Cities by Dickens.

clue.text: Monarch protects following pages from this bully

indicators.note: protects means one piece wraps round and shields the other

parts.note: a monarch is a ruler
ff is the abbreviation for following pages

explanation.surface: A king shields subsequent pages of a book from a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffler was a swaggering vagabond or ruffian, an old word for a thug.

clue.text: Thus diluted beer is not drunk

parts.note: thus means so

indicators.note: diluted means weakened, so beer loses some of its substance, one letter

explanation.surface: Watered-down beer won't get anyone intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diluted' takes an E from BEER, leaving BER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober describes someone free of alcohol's effects.

clue.text: Lassie and I rambling in Europe

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters of Lassie and I go astray

explanation.surface: A dog named Lassie and her owner walking across the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historic region of central Europe, now mostly in Poland.

clue.text: Delivered nothing by rail

parts.note: BR is British Rail
ought, a variant of nought, means nothing

explanation.surface: Goods handed over without charge by train.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stood for British Rail, the former UK national railway; 'by' puts it beside OUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought is the past tense of bring, the same as carried or handed over.

clue.text: A few difficult to control

definitions.meaning: an unruly person, especially a child

explanation.surface: Several hard-to-manage people.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful is a small quantity and also a person who is a trial to manage.

clue.text: Nothing less will do?

parts.note: reads as insisting on the maximum, but asks for the smallest amount, with nothing below it

explanation.surface: A demand that only the very best is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the amount than which nothing is smaller.

clue.text: Old ships out East making large amounts

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is dropped from the ships

parts.note: galleons were old sailing ships
E is East

explanation.surface: Ancient ships heading eastward brought great quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallons, measures of liquid, is used loosely for lots.

clue.text: Two girls one on each knee

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name
Ella is another girl's name

explanation.surface: Two girls each sitting on someone's lap, one per knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two girls' gives two names, PAT and ELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a bone found in both legs.

clue.text: Missile coming out of S African wood

definitions.meaning: a South African tree whose wood is used for spear shafts

explanation.surface: A projectile emerging from a South African forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The assegai is a Zulu throwing spear and also the cornel-like tree of the Cape from which shafts are made.

clue.text: Intimate talk between a couple of cards

definitions.meaning: placed between two cards of one red suit

explanation.surface: A private conversation over a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a candid chat, and split up the words show a TO between two red-suit cards.
